claims.text: The as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi films have an ordered, single-phase hexagonal structure.
The as-deposited films contain residual microstrain.
The as-deposited films have a high density of grain boundaries that act as magnetic-domain pinning sites.
Residual microstrain and grain-boundary pinning govern the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films.
Microstructural defects stabilize a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition in these films.
A short post-deposition anneal at approximately 400 degrees Celsius will relieve residual microstrain.
Controlled annealing will decrease the density of defect-rich grain boundaries.
Reducing microstrain and grain-boundary defects will reduce domain-wall pinning during the magnetostructural transition.
Reduced domain-wall pinning will lower hysteretic energy losses.
Reduced microstrain and pinning will produce a broader, more gradual entropy change.
Annealing can leave the films single phase without secondary-phase formation.
The annealed films will have smaller magnetic-hysteresis loop areas and lower coercivity than the as-deposited films.
The annealed films will exhibit a broader transition-temperature range than the as-deposited films.
The thin-film form will retain enhanced potential for rapid heat exchange after annealing.
The predicted benefits hold only within an annealing window that avoids secondary-phase formation and excessive grain coarsening.
Outside the proposed annealing window, the beneficial effects may be lost or reversed.
Post-deposition rapid thermal annealing has been studied in an analogous high-entropy-alloy thin-film system.
Direct evidence connecting microstrain relief to reduced hysteresis in FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloys is limited.
The optimal annealing temperature and duration for balancing heat exchange and hysteresis are not established.
Failure to reduce hysteresis or broaden the transition while retaining the same phase would falsify the hypothesis.
